title: Multiplying and dividing decimals by 10 and 100
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: Multiplying or dividing a decimal by 10 or 100 is quick once you know the trick: you just slide the decimal point.
To multiply a decimal by 10, move the decimal point one place to the RIGHT; by 100, move it two places right.

steps: Move the point one place right.

blocks.explain: Moving the point one place right turns 3.4 into 34.
blocks.rule: To multiply by 10 move the point one place right; by 100 move it two places right.

blocks.content: To divide a decimal by 10, move the decimal point one place to the LEFT; by 100, move it two places left.

blocks.explain: Moving the point one place left turns 34 into 3.4.
blocks.rule: To divide by 10 move the point one place left; by 100 move it two places left.

blocks.question: Sam says 0.2 x 0.3 = 0.6. Is he right?
options: No — 0.2 x 0.3 = 0.06, because there are two decimal places
blocks.explain: Multiply the digits: 2 x 3 = 6. Now count the decimal places in the question: 0.2 has one and 0.3 has one, so two altogether. Put two decimal places in the answer: 0.06. A tenth of a tenth is small.
blocks.rule: Multiply the digits, then give the answer as many decimal places as the two factors have together.
blocks.principle: Multiplying two small decimals gives an even smaller decimal.
canonical_solution: So the answer has 2 decimal places

rubric.look_for: multiplies 2 x 3 and counts decimal places
explains why the product is smaller than each factor

misconceptions.coach: Count the decimal places: two, so 0.06 not 0.6.
Only two decimal places are needed, not three.

practiceItems.prompt: decimal places in the answer to 0.2 x 0.3

blocks.content: Times 10 or 100 slides the point right; divide by 10 or 100 slides it left. Count the zeros to count the places. Let's practise!
